newsitem.title: USA: Toy retailers upbeat about holiday season.
newsitem.headline: Toy retailers upbeat about holiday season.

text.p: Toy retailers are optimistic this year as "back-to-basics" toys such as trucks, dolls and board games are expected to do well compared with electronic toys.
"We're expecting this to be the best Christmas of the '90s," Brooke Adkins, vice president of marketing at FAO Schwarz, said in a telephone interview.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc, FAO Schwarz and other retailers see classic toys like Barbie and Star Wars figurines topping Christmas lists.
Many of the toys that are popular this holiday season are toys that were popular when baby boomers were children, Adkins said.
FAO Schwarz, a unit of the Koninklidjke Bijenkorf Beheer (KBB) Dutch retail chain, is expecting "double digit same-store sales improvements over the year ago period," Adkins said.
Adkins declined to give a specific range, but described the 39-store chain's prospects this season as "very healthy."
The new Holiday Barbie "has been going off the shelves the moment we stock them," said Sharon Weber, a Wal-Mart spokeswoman said.
Wal-Mart declined to comment on sales growth expectations, but said "we expect it will be a good season," Weber said.

Dare Johnston, a district manager at Consolidated Stores Corp's Kay Bee unit, said the chain is expecting an improved holiday season and there are early signs that shoppers are spending more this year than last year.
In electronic toy sales, Nintendo's 64-bit video game player is expected to sell well. Some shoppers noted that stores have had trouble keeping video game systems in stock.
Hollywood is expected to drive some toy sales with toys based upon Walt Disney Co's "101 Dalmations" and Time Warner Inc's "Space Jam."
"We expect them to be popular, but nothing in the league with Power Rangers or Cabbage Patch Dolls," FAO Schwarz's Adkins said.
Toys R Us, the largest U.S. toy retailer, declined to talk about its sales or sales projections. A spokeswoman for the company said November and December are their blackout periods.
-- Bill Borden, New York News Desk (212)-859-1700
